sources.title: Entry to the Faroe Islands or Greenland
sources.officialityEvidence: The Danish Immigration Service publishes this current territorial entry guidance on its official nyidanmark.dk government site; it was last updated 27 July 2026.
sources.supportingExcerpt: If you can enter Denmark without a visa, you can also enter the Faroe Islands and Greenland without a visa.

sources.title: Countries with a visa requirement and visa-free countries
sources.officialityEvidence: The official Danish Immigration Service register states its visa-required and visa-free nationality lists and passport qualifications; it was last updated 24 July 2025.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Below you find a list of countries with a visa requirement and visa-free countries.

sources.title: Visa-free travel
sources.officialityEvidence: The Danish Immigration Service expressly extends these visa-free entry conditions and the combined stay calculation to the Faroe Islands and Greenland.
sources.supportingExcerpt: You may stay in the Schengen region and in Greenland and on the Faroe Islands for a maximum combined of 90 days.

sources.title: Executive Order on Aliens' Access to Denmark on the Basis of a Visa
sources.publisher: Ministry of Immigration and Integration of Denmark
sources.officialityEvidence: The Danish Immigration Service hosts the Ministry's English translation of the current Visa Executive Order, in force from 24 November 2025.
sources.supportingExcerpt: A visa issued according to the rules in this executive order is not valid for the Faroe Islands or Greenland.

policies.title: Nordic nationals: permit-free entry, residence and work
policies.summary: Danish, Finnish, Icelandic, Norwegian and Swedish nationals may enter, reside and work in the Faroe Islands without a permit; this records their ordinary-passport short-visitor outcome as visa-free.
conditions: The territory-specific source states that Nordic nationals can enter, reside and work without a permit. This does not classify any pair as citizenship because the catalog has no Faroe Islands passport issuer code.
Final identity, security, sanctions and border-control checks remain applicable.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: These listed passport holders may enter Denmark visa-free and therefore, under the current Danish territorial rule, may enter the Faroe Islands visa-free for a short visit.
conditions: Visa-free travel is limited to a maximum combined 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen region, Greenland and the Faroe Islands, subject to the stated special Danish calculations for specified nationalities.
A valid travel document, documented purpose and sufficient means are required; refusal, SIS, expulsion, UN/EU sanctions and final border-admission checks apply.
This policy does not establish work, residence, diplomatic, service, special, emergency, refugee, crew or other-document treatment.

policies.title: Named biometric ordinary passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: The Danish official register exempts these named nationalities only when the stated biometric-passport condition is met; the current territorial rule carries that visa-free result to the Faroe Islands.
conditions: A biometric ordinary passport is required. The register gives issue-date information for Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine; Georgia's ordinary passports issued from 28 July 2014 are biometric.
The same combined 90-days-in-180 visa-free maximum, travel-document, purpose, means, sanctions and final-admission conditions apply.

policies.title: Hong Kong, Macao and qualifying Taiwan passports: visa-free visitor entry
policies.summary: The Danish register's passport-specific exemptions carry to the Faroe Islands under the current territorial entry rule.
conditions: Hong Kong requires an HKSAR passport and Macao requires a Macao SAR passport. Taiwan requires the stated identity-card number, and older Republic of China passports also require stated Taiwan birthplace and identity-card number.
The policy is visa-free only under the stated document qualifications and ordinary short-visitor conditions; it does not infer a nationality or citizenship classification from a catalog code.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: Faroe Islands visitor visa required
policies.summary: These passports are in Denmark's current visa-required nationality schedule without an applicable ordinary-passport exemption and need a visa valid for the Faroe Islands before a short visit.
conditions: The visa sticker must expressly be valid for the Faroe Islands. A Danish/Schengen visa alone does not authorize entry to the Faroe Islands; the standard application and issue route is through a Danish diplomatic mission or Danish representation abroad.
A territorial Faroe Islands visa can authorize a stay of up to 90 days. That territorial-visa maximum is distinct from the combined visa-free 90-days-in-180 calculation.
Online filing does not itself establish an eVisa. An individual border visa may exceptionally be issued under the applicable rules; it does not establish a passport-wide visa-on-arrival route.

A physical residence permit or EU free-movement residence card issued by Denmark, another EU country or another Schengen country is a separate document-conditioned no-visa route. A C or D visa from another Schengen country alone is insufficient unless territorially endorsed; exceptional entry-permit routes do not alter this passport baseline.

Diplomatic, service, official, special, residence, work, transit, refugee and other travel-document exceptions are outside this ordinary-passport policy; visa issuance and final admission remain discretionary.

conflicts.explanation: The current Danish register exempts Kosovo citizens holding biometric passports, and the territorial entry guidance extends Denmark visa-free entry to the Faroe Islands.
